title: Console: surface batching tier selection + effective defaults/explainers
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal
Expose the new batching tier concept (fast / standard / cost-efficient) in Redwood Console so customers can:
1) Select a tier per deployment / route config.
2) Understand the *effective* batching parameters that will be applied (computed defaults + any explicit overrides).
3) Navigate to docs explaining trade-offs and troubleshooting.

Context
Runtime is introducing workload-aware tiered batching defaults. We need Console to be the “single source of truth” UI for:
- Selecting batching_tier (fast|standard|cost_efficient)
- Showing computed defaults returned by the control plane / runtime explain endpoint
- Highlighting precedence (explicit knobs override tier defaults)

Scope (Console)
- Add a “Batching profile” control to the deployment/route configuration panel.
- Add an “Effective batching config” read-only section driven by the explain endpoint.
- Add inline explainers and doc links.
- Track basic analytics events for adoption + confusion points.

Out of scope
- Authoring custom per-customer optimized profiles beyond the three tiers.
- Visualizing per-request batch formation in Console (covered by dashboards).

Proposed UX
1) Field: “Batching profile”
   - Dropdown values:
     - Fast (lowest p95 latency)
     - Standard (recommended)
     - Cost-efficient (lower $/token)
   - Secondary helper text: “Applies safe defaults based on model + hardware. You can still override specific knobs below.”
   - If no tier explicitly set (inherit behavior), show “Standard (recommended)” as the displayed default *but* persist as unset unless user changes it (to avoid unintentional config diffs on edit).

2) Effective batching config (read-only)
   - Show a compact table of the effective values returned by /explain (or equivalent) for the selected model + SKU:
     - max_batch_size
     - max_queue_delay_ms
     - prefill_decode_ratio (or separate weights)
     - kv_cache_pressure_limit
     - admission_control_mode
     - overload_protection_thresholds (high level summary only)
   - Highlight any fields that are explicitly overridden in the saved config.
   - Include a “Copy effective config” action for support/debugging.

3) Precedence / explainers
   - Add an info tooltip: “Explicit settings override tier defaults. If you set max_queue_delay_ms manually, the tier will not adjust it automatically.”
   - Add a link: “Learn about batching tiers” -> docs (owned by DevEx; see ENG-18426 / docs PR).

4) Empty/error states
   - If explain endpoint is unavailable or returns error:
     - Show tier dropdown normally (config editing still works)
     - Show effective config card with a non-blocking warning: “Unable to fetch computed defaults. Try again or check runtime/control plane status.”
   - If user selects Cost-efficient tier on streaming routes, show a warning banner (non-blocking): “Streaming cadence may be impacted; validate token cadence metrics and consider Standard/Fast for user-facing streaming.” (copy TBD w/ Product)

Acceptance criteria
- User can set batching_tier in Console and it is persisted in config export/import.
- Effective batching config renders for at least:
  - Hosted API routes: chat/completions + embeddings (where applicable)
  - Dedicated deployments (config page)
  - Private deployments (where Console is present) when explain endpoint is enabled
- Effective config reflects precedence correctly:
  - If user sets explicit knobs, UI indicates they override tier defaults.
  - If user removes explicit override, effective config reverts to tier-derived values after refresh.
- Doc link present and points to the stable docs URL (no Confluence links in customer-facing UI).
- Instrumentation:
  - Emit event when tier dropdown is changed (include old/new tier + route type).
  - Emit event when “Copy effective config” is used.
- Feature flag:
  - UI behind a console feature flag (default off in prod until runtime flag ramp is approved).

Implementation notes
- Data source: prefer the new explain endpoint added in sources/github/redwood/pr_18470.json.
- Avoid duplicating tier-to-parameter logic in Console. Console should treat the explain response as authoritative.
- Caching: OK to cache explain response for 30–60s keyed by (deployment_id, route_id, model, sku, tier, explicit_overrides_hash) to reduce load when user is iterating on UI.

Open questions
- Naming: confirm customer-facing copy for “Cost-efficient” vs “Eco” (Product thread indicates ‘cost-efficient’).
- Where to show tier selection: per-route only vs also at deployment-level default. Current assumption: per-route selection with optional deployment default later.

References
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/workload-aware-batching-defaults-prd.json
- Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/workload-aware-batching-defaults-design-spec.json
- Runtime explain endpoint: sources/github/redwood/pr_18470.json
- DevEx docs plan: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/batching-profiles-docs-plan.json
- SLO tiers (for copy + warnings): sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/latency-slo-tiers-fast-standard-costefficient.json
